Field Entry 
Source ID WBC-0005 
Title Generation Rate and Particle Size Distribution of Wood Dust by Handheld Sanding Operation 
Source type Paper 
Link / File DOI: 10.1539/joh.16-0136-BR 
Craft 
applicability Wood (likely comparable for bamboo dust, though not directly tested) 
Primary Why-
theme 8. Dust and Respiratory Exposure 
Process stage Finishing (machine paper-finishing + final hand sanding) 
Questions 
answered / 
generated 
Why does sanding — machine or hand — generate significant airborne 
wood dust? What quantity and particle size of dust is produced during 
handheld sanding? 
Evidence level E3 (direct scientific evidence, measured exposure data) 
Relevance note 
IIT process documentation confirms the Udayagiri sequence uses a 
powered paper-finishing machine followed by a final manual hand-sanding 
step. This study directly measures exposure from powered handheld 
sanding, closely matching the machine-finishing stage; it serves as a 
reasonable but indirect proxy for the subsequent manual hand-sanding 
stage, where dust generation is expected to be lower but has not been 
separately measured.

Source ID WBC-0004 
Title The Mechanics of Splitting Wood and the Design of Neolithic Woodworking Tools 
Source type Paper (peer-reviewed, open access) 
Link / File https://exarc.net/issue-2017-4/ea/mechanics-splitting-wood-and-design-neolithic-woodworking-tools 
Craft 
applicability 
Wood (handle/socket construction — applies to wood and bamboo tool 
handles) 
Primary Why-
theme 
10. Failure, Repair and Quality (with a secondary link to 7. Tools and tool-
material interaction) 
Process stage Tool maintenance / primary shaping (tool condition affecting all carving stages) 
Questions 
answered / 
generated 
Why does the tool handle split near the socket under repeated impact? 
Why does a metal ring or flange at the socket reduce this failure? 
Evidence level E3 (direct scientific evidence, experimentally validated model) 
Relevance note 
Explains the mechanics of radial wood splitting at handle/socket junctions 
under impact and shows why reinforcing collars/flanges at the socket 
reduce failure — directly supporting the artisan practice of fitting an iron 
ring to the neem handle of the baria.

Source ID WBC-0008 
Title Stress Concentration around Circular and Elliptic Holes in Wood Laminates 
Source type Paper 
Link / File https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339301496 
Craft 
applicability Wood 
Primary Why-
theme 10. Failure, Repair and Quality 
Process stage Piercing / opening refinement / nakshi cutting 
Questions 
answered / 
generated 
Why does a narrow bridge of wood between pierced openings break? Why 
does hole spacing and shape affect the strength of the remaining wood 
around it? 
Evidence 
level E3 (direct scientific evidence, anisotropic wood-specific stress analysis) 
Relevance 
note 
Analyzes how wood's natural anisotropy affects stress concentration around 
circular and elliptic holes, providing a mechanical basis for why narrow 
bridges between pierced openings in nakshi/openwork designs are prone to 
fracture, especially depending on hole spacing, shape, and grain direction.

Source ID WBC-0009 
Title 
Effect of Grain Angle on the Strain Distribution During Orthogonal Cutting of 
Hinoki (Chamaecyparis obtusa) Measured Using a Digital Image Correlation 
Method 
Source type Paper (open access) 
Link / File https://jwoodscience.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s10086-019-1824-2 
Craft 
applicability Wood 
Primary 
Why-theme 10. Failure, Repair and Quality 
Process stage Primary shaping / rough carving 
Questions 
answered / 
generated 
Why does cutting against or across the grain produce torn or fuzzy grain? 
Why does grain angle affect surface tear-out during carving? 
Evidence 
level 
E3 (direct scientific evidence, strain measurement via digital image 
correlation) 
Relevance 
note 
Directly measures how grain angle relative to the tool path governs strain 
and cleavage ahead of the cutting edge, providing a mechanical explanation 
for the torn-grain and fuzzy-grain defects recorded during primary shaping 
and carving of Udayagiri wood.

Field Entry 
Source ID WBC-0010 
Title Microstructure and Mechanism of Grain Raising in Wood 
Source type Paper (open access) 
Link / File DOI: 10.3390/coatings7090135 
Craft 
applicability Wood 
Primary Why-
theme 
11. Product Function, Use and Performance (with secondary link to 10. 
Failure, Repair and Quality) 
Process stage Finishing (sanding) / product use (wetting) 
Questions 
answered / 
generated 
Why does a sanded wood surface become rough again after wetting? Why 
are some wood species more prone to grain raising than others? 
Evidence level E3 (direct scientific evidence, profilometry and SEM characterization) 
Relevance note 
Shows that sanding tears cell walls to create loosely bonded fibre slivers 
that project after wetting, and that grain raising is inversely related to 
wood density — directly explaining why finished Udayagiri surfaces 
(spoons, bowls, handles) may roughen again after washing, and suggesting 
species density as a relevant factor for food-contact product performance.

Source ID WBC-0011 
Title 21 CFR Part 175 — Indirect Food Additives: Adhesives and Components of Coatings 
Source type Regulation / Official government standard 
Link / File https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-175 
Craft 
applicability Wood (food-contact repair; applies to any food-contact craft object) 
Primary Why-
theme 10. Repair (Failure, Repair and Quality) 
Process stage Post-production repair / final inspection 
Questions 
answered / 
generated 
Why can't any adhesive or filler be used to repair a food-contact object? 
What conditions must an adhesive meet to be safely used on such a 
product? 
Evidence level E2 (official regulatory/standards evidence, not experimental science) 
Relevance note 
Establishes the legal/regulatory conditions under which adhesives and 
coatings may be used on food-contact articles, directly addressing the craft 
report's flagged concern that repair materials for spoons and bowls require 
documented suitability evidence before use.

Source ID WBC-0012 
Title New Formaldehyde-Free Adhesives for Wood Manufacturing: In Vitro Evaluation of Potential Toxicity of Fine Dust from Wood Sawing 
Source type Paper 
Link / File PMID: 34968639 
Craft 
applicability Wood 
Primary Why-
theme 10. Repair (Failure, Repair and Quality) 
Process stage Repair / adhesive selection 
Questions 
answered / 
generated 
Why does the chemical composition of a wood adhesive matter for safety? 
Why might formaldehyde-based adhesives pose a health risk compared to 
alternatives? 
Evidence level E3 (direct scientific evidence, in vitro toxicology; indirect proxy for food-contact migration specifically) 
Relevance note 
Provides experimental toxicity evidence that adhesive chemistry (e.g., 
formaldehyde-based resins) carries real health risk via dust/emissions, 
supporting the broader reasoning behind the report's caution on repair-
material selection. Note: this study addresses inhalation exposure during 
sawing, not direct food-contact migration — it complements but does not 
replace the WBC-0011 regulatory source.

Source ID WBC-0003 
Title The Influence of Hand Tool Design on Hand Grip Strength: A Review 
Source type Paper (review) 
Link / File https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336677500 
Craft 
applicability Wood (tool ergonomics — applies to both wood and bamboo carving tools) 
Primary Why-
theme 7. Posture, Grip and Body Mechanics 
Process stage Primary shaping / carving 
Questions 
answered / 
generated 
Why does handle diameter and material affect grip force and hand fatigue? 
Why might a mismatched handle size increase strain during prolonged tool 
use? 
Evidence level E3 (direct scientific evidence) 
Relevance 
note 
The review synthesizes multiple studies showing handle diameter and 
material as the most significant hand-tool design factors affecting grip 
strength and fatigue, providing scientific grounding for interpreting the 
baria's neem-wood handle and its ergonomic role for the artisan.

Source ID WBC-0007 
Title Risk Factors Associated with Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders Among Floor-Sitting Precision Handicraft Workers 
Source type Paper 
Link / File DOI: 10.1007/s00420-021-01817-5 
Craft 
applicability 
Wood (Indian handicraft precision-work posture; applicable across floor-
seated craft trades) 
Primary Why-
theme 7. Posture, Grip and Body Mechanics 
Process stage Rough/fine carving (visually demanding, sustained near-body handwork) 
Questions 
answered / 
generated 
Why does prolonged, close, floor-seated carving posture increase risk to 
the neck, back and knees? Why do continuous work without breaks and 
sustained awkward posture increase MSD risk? 
Evidence level 
E3 (direct scientific evidence, occupational cross-sectional study using 
RULA/REBA and Nordic questionnaire on Indian precision handicraft 
workers) 
Relevance note 
Confirms high MSD prevalence (neck 61.6%, lower back 74.8%, knee 
54.7%) among floor-sitting Indian precision handicraft workers, and 
identifies sustained awkward posture, prolonged hours, and lack of breaks 
as key risk factors — directly applicable to the close, seated hand-carving 
posture documented for Udayagiri artisans.

Source ID WBC-0014 
Title 
A Study on Monitoring of Frying Performance and Oxidative Stability of 
Virgin Coconut Oil (VCO) During Continuous/Prolonged Deep Fat Frying 
Process Using Chemical and FTIR Spectroscopy 
Source type Paper 
Link / File DOI: 10.1007/s13197-013-1078-8 
Craft 
applicability Wood (surface-treatment oil used on food-contact Udayagiri products) 
Primary Why-
theme 11. Product Function, Use and Performance 
Process stage Final treatment (oil application) 
Questions 
answered / 
generated 
Why can't coconut oil's food-safe status alone guarantee it is a stable long-
term wood finish? Why might oil-treated food-contact objects need 
regular reapplication or maintenance? 
Evidence level E3 (direct scientific evidence, chemical/FTIR measurement of oxidative degradation) 
Relevance note 
Directly measures that virgin coconut oil's free fatty acid content and 
peroxide value increase significantly with prolonged heat/time exposure, 
evidencing progressive oxidative degradation — supporting the report's 
caution that coconut oil's performance as a wood finish on food-contact 
Udayagiri products (repeated washing, storage, use) requires separate 
testing rather than assumption from its edibility.

Source type Paper 
Link / File DOI: 10.5552/drind.2014.1335

Process stage Cutting

generated

Evidence level E3 
Relevance note 
The study experimentally investigates wood-splitting force and shows

Source type Paper

Source ID WBC-0006 
Title Assessment of Low-Cost Intervention (Foam Rubber) Among Wood Carvers Exposed to Hand-Arm Vibration and Noise 
Source type Paper 
Link / File https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333161422 
Craft 
applicability 
Wood (Indian handicraft wood-carving sector; likely comparable for bamboo 
carving) 
Primary Why-
theme 9. Vibration (with secondary link to Noise) 
Process stage Rough carving / primary shaping (hand-tool use) 
Questions 
answered / 
generated 
Why does prolonged hand-tool carving expose artisans to hand-arm 
vibration and high noise levels? Why might a damping handle intervention 
reduce this exposure? 
Evidence 
level 
E3 (direct scientific evidence, field-measured exposure data from Indian 
wood carvers) 
Relevance 
note 
Directly measures HAV and noise exposure (mean Lex,8h of 93.17 dB(A), 
exceeding safe limits) among Indian wood carvers using hand carving tools, 
and tests a low-cost foam-rubber handle intervention showing ~20% 
vibration reduction — closely matching the baria/ulli hand-tool use 
documented for Udayagiri artisans.

Source ID WBC-0013 
Title SPSS Analysis for Predicting the Occupational Health and Safety of Sawmill Workers in the Wood Processing Industries in Kerala, India 
Source type Paper 
Link / File https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s43621-025-01440-1 
Craft 
applicability 
Wood (Indian wood-processing machinery; sanding/machine-noise relevant 
to Udayagiri's powered stages) 
Primary Why-
theme 8. Noise (with secondary link to Dust) 
Process stage Piercing/drilling (electric drill) and machine-assisted surface refinement 
Questions 
answered / 
generated 
Why do powered wood-processing machines (drilling, sanding) pose a noise-
induced hearing loss risk? What noise levels are typical at Indian wood-
processing workstations? 
Evidence level E3 (direct scientific evidence, on-site dBA measurement and audiometry in an Indian wood-processing setting) 
Relevance 
note 
Measures actual machine noise levels and audiometric hearing outcomes 
among Indian wood-processing workers using drilling and sanding 
equipment comparable to Udayagiri's electric drill and paper-finishing 
machine, directly addressing the report's flagged gap that no local noise 
measurement exists.

Source ID WBC-0017 
Title Effects of Mixed Hardwoods Dust on Respiratory Function and Blood Immunoglobulin Levels in Wood Workers 
Source type Paper (open access) 
Link https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10884841/ 
Craft 
applicability 
Wood (tropical hardwood — directly matches ebony/rosewood/sandalwood 
dust profile) 
Primary 
Why-theme 8. Dust and Respiratory Exposure 
Process 
stage Phase II & III: Shaping, filing, sanding 
Questions 
answered 
Why does dense tropical hardwood dust pose a greater respiratory risk than 
ordinary sawdust? 
Evidence 
level E3 
Relevance 
note 
Measured, significant reduction in lung function (VC, FEV1, PEFR) and 
elevated IgE/IgG in workers exposed to mixed tropical hardwood dust — 
directly relevant since Delhi's material palette (ebony, sandalwood, red 
sandalwood) is exactly this category of wood.

Source ID WBC-0018 
Title Drying and Control of Moisture Content and Dimensional Changes 
Source type Technical report / handbook chapter (peer-reviewed government research) 
Link https://www.researchgate.net/publication/285852322 
Craft 
applicability Wood (general — applies across all species, especially dense hardwoods) 
Primary 
Why-theme 10. Failure, Repair and Quality 
Process 
stage Storage / post-completion (finished-object stability) 
Questions 
answered 
Why does seasonal humidity variation cause finished wood objects to crack 
or warp? 
Evidence 
level E3/E4 (authoritative technical reference, not a single experiment) 
Relevance 
note 
Explains that wood continuously exchanges moisture with its environment 
and that seasonal (not daily) humidity swings are the main driver of 
dimensional change and cracking — directly supporting Delhi's flagged need 
for humidity-controlled storage of finished carvings.

Source type Paper 
Link / File https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363545397 
Craft 
applicability Wood (applies to any hand-repeated precision craft task) 
Primary 
Why-theme 10. Quality (distinct from Failure) 
Process

Questions 
answered 
Why does hand-carved symmetry vary between repeated pieces, even by a 
skilled artisan? 
Evidence 
level E3 
Relevance 
note 
Confirms motor variability is an inherent, measurable feature of human 
repetitive manual precision tasks, providing a scientific basis for the report's 
observation of symmetry inconsistency across repeated hand-carved designs.

Title Analyzing the Impact of Veneer Layup Direction and Heat Treatment on Plywood Strain Distribution During Bending Load by DIC Technique 
Source type Paper 
Link / File https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2238785423027540 
Craft 
applicability Wood (engineered wood/veneer hybrid construction) 
Primary 
Why-theme 11. Product Function, Use and Performance 
Process

Questions 
answered 
Why does layering a thin premium veneer over a laminated core affect the

note 
Shows that veneer layup angle and layer arrangement directly govern strain

for evaluating whether Delhi's proposed LVL-core-plus-veneer strategy will 
achieve the "improved material stability" it claims, rather than assuming it 
from cost/visual benefits alone.

Source ID
WBC-0031
Title
Wood Dust Particle and Mass Concentrations and Filtration Efficiency in
Sanding of Wood Materials
Source type
Paper
Link / File
https://www.researchgate.net/publication/23640758
Craft applicability
Wood (tropical hardwood species — relevant to teak, jackfruit used in
Kallakurichi)
Primary Why-theme
8. Dust and Respiratory Exposure
Process stage
Proposed mechanization (rotary tools, angle grinder discs)
Questions answered
Why would introducing rotary/grinding power tools increase fine and
respirable dust exposure compared to hand tools?
Evidence level
E3
Relevance note
Shows that denser tropical hardwoods generate a higher proportion of
fine, respirable dust particles (PM10, PM2.5, PM1) during power
sanding/grinding, indicating that the report's proposed mechanization
tools (angle grinder, rotary tools) would introduce a new dust exposure
risk not present in the current hand-tool process.

Title
In Situ Construction of Thermotropic Shape Memory Polymer in Wood for
Enhancing Its Dimensional Stability
Source type
Paper
Link / File
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8876273/
Craft applicability
Wood (moisture-prone species — Noni and Albizia lebbeck used in
Kallakurichi carving)
Primary Why-theme
10. Failure, Repair and Quality
Process stage
Material augmentation (pre/post-carving treatment)
Questions answered
Why does vacuum-pressure resin impregnation reduce warping and
cracking in moisture-prone wood species?
Evidence level
E3
Relevance note
Demonstrates that vacuum-pressure impregnation of resin into wood cell
lumens significantly enhances dimensional stability and reduces
cracking, supporting the report's proposal to use vacuum-aided resin
infusion on moisture-prone species like Noni and Albizia lebbeck.

Title
Improvement of Termite Resistance, Dimensional Stability and
Mechanical Properties of Pine Wood by Paraffin Impregnation
Source type
Paper

https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00107-014-0823-7
Craft applicability
Wood (moisture-prone species — Noni, Albizia lebbeck, teak used in
Kallakurichi)
Primary Why-theme

Process stage
Material augmentation (post-carving preservation treatment)
Questions answered
Why does paraffin wax impregnation improve a wood object's resistance

Evidence level

Directly demonstrates that paraffin-impregnated wood shows improved
equilibrium moisture content, dimensional stability, density, bending
strength, and termite resistance compared to untreated wood, supporting
the report's proposal to use a paraffin wax barrier for long-term pest and
decay resistance on high-value carved species.

Title
Comparative Analysis of Methods for Plastification of Solid Wood
Source type
Paper
Link / File
https://www.researchgate.net/publication/312498200
Craft applicability
Wood (Kallakurichi diesel/solvent-based fiber softening before fine
detailing)
Primary Why-theme
11. Product Function, Use and Performance
Process stage
Diesel addition (post rough-shaping softening step)
Questions answered
Why does applying a solvent (diesel, or the proposed isopropyl
alcohol/water alternative) to wood reduce the force needed for fine
carving and reduce cracking/splintering?
Evidence level
E3
Relevance note
Explains that moisture/solvent content directly governs the plastic

its protection and longevity beyond the natural finish?
Evidence level

Relevance note
An Indian Institute of Wood Science study found shellac-based varnishes
gave up to 100% termite resistance for 6 months and improved
fungal/borer resistance, supporting why varnish is offered as an optional
protective final finish, while explaining why many artisans still prefer the
natural unvarnished finish for aesthetic reasons.
